stories.article_text_excerpt: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5Nm2x Image: Britta Pedersen/dpa/picture alliance Advertisement What you need to know about plague There are three forms of plague, all caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis. The three forms of plague are bubonic, septicemic and pneumonic. Bubonic plague is the most common form, it does not spread from person to person. If untreated, the bacteria can move through the body and bloodstream, causing septicemic plague, which causes internal bleeding and organ failure. If the the bacteria reach the lungs, they cause pneumonic plague. Pneumonic plague is highly contagious as it can pass from person to person through the air, via coughing, for example. If untreated, bubonic plague kills between 30-60% of patients. The septicemic and pneumonic forms are always fatal without treatment.
